newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds lower in cautious market.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds lower in cautious market.

text.p: Argentine bonds were lower at midsession Thursday, still affected by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks that U.S. share prices were too high and eyeing an imminent Fed meeting for any clue about rates, dealers said.
"Local news have no impact (on bond markets), only the international ones have it," said Ignacio Lafuente, sales trader at Banco Frances.
The FRB was down 3/8 at 84-3/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.20 to 121.6.
"I see caution from now until the Fed meeting on December 19. I don't see any recovery," Lafuente added. "Argentine pension funds are barely active."
Oscar Falleroni, director of Banco de Galicia investment fund, said: "There may still be a slight downward correction.

"With the U.S. long bond rate firm at 6.61 percent and a possible slight rates hike by the Fed, emerging market bonds may fall. And with good results so far some fund managers could sell emerging markets to take positions in U.S. bonds."
